title: Curcumol Ameliorates Cisplatin-induced Nephrotoxicity by Targeting TAK1 and Inhibiting MAPK and NF-kappaB Pathways.
authors: Jin, Xuejin; Yuan, Miao; Wang, Lingkun; Zha, Huiyan; Zheng, Zhiwei; Xu, Zheng; Shi, Jing; Liang, Guang; Zhou, Qian
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究姜黄素靶向TAK1抑制MAPK/NF-κB通路减轻顺铂肾毒性，核心为小分子-蛋白互作与信号通路，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although cisplatin (Cis) is a foundational chemotherapeutic agent, its dose-limiting nephrotoxicity lacks clinically effective drugs. Curcumol (CUR), a bioactive sesquiterpenoid derived from Curcuma zedoariae rhizome, exhibits multi-organ protective effects. However, its therapeutic potential and molecular targets in Cis-provoked acute kidney injury (AKI) remain unexplored. PURPOSE: This study systematically investigated the nephroprotection and underlying mechanism of CUR in Cis-induced nephrotoxicity. METHODS: C57BL/6 mice received intraperitoneal administration of 20 mg/kg Cis to induce AKI. Dual-concentration CUR (40/80 mg/kg) was administered pre- and post-treatment in Cis-challenged mice, with longitudinal monitoring of renal function. Human tubular epithelial cells (HK-2 cells) were used to evaluate CUR's nephroprotection in vitro. RNA-sequencing transcriptomics identified pathway-level mechanisms, while structure-based molecular docking (MOD) prioritized target proteins. RESULTS: CUR exhibited dose-responsive nephroprotection, reducing apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammation more effectively than N-acetylcysteine in pre- and post-Cis treatment regimens. Mechanistically, we revealed that nephroprotection of CUR primarily involves suppression of phosphorylation-mediated MAPK/NF-kappaB pathway activation, thereby mitigating the inflammatory response. Notably, MOD and Cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) data suggested a direct interaction between CUR and TAK1. Functional validation experiments demonstrated that TAK1 silencing attenuated cisplatin-induced tubular cell injury, and TAK1 activity was essential for CUR's protective effects. CONCLUSION: CUR ameliorated Cis-triggered AKI by targeting TAK1 and inhibiting MAPK and NF-kappaB pathways. These findings suggest that CUR may serve as a promising adjuvant to overcome the primary limitation of Cis.
abstract_zh: 背景：尽管顺铂（Cis）是一种基础性化疗药物，但其剂量限制性肾毒性缺乏临床有效的治疗药物。莪术醇（CUR）是一种源自莪术根茎的生物活性倍半萜类化合物，具有多器官保护作用。然而，其在顺铂诱发的急性肾损伤（AKI）中的治疗潜力和分子靶点尚未被探索。目的：本研究系统探讨了CUR在顺铂诱导的肾毒性中的肾脏保护作用及其潜在机制。方法：C57BL/6小鼠接受腹腔注射20 mg/kg顺铂以诱导AKI。在顺铂攻击的小鼠中，采用双浓度CUR（40/80 mg/kg）进行预处理和后处理，并纵向监测肾功能。使用人肾小管上皮细胞（HK-2细胞）评估CUR在体外的肾脏保护作用。RNA测序转录组学鉴定了通路水平机制，而基于结构的分子对接（MOD）则优先筛选靶蛋白。结果：CUR表现出剂量依赖性的肾脏保护作用，在顺铂预处理和后处理方案中，其减少凋亡、氧化应激和炎症的效果优于N-乙酰半胱氨酸。机制上，我们揭示CUR的肾脏保护作用主要涉及抑制磷酸化介导的MAPK/NF-kappaB通路激活，从而减轻炎症反应。值得注意的是，MOD和细胞热位移分析（CETSA）数据提示CUR与TAK1之间存在直接相互作用。功能验证实验表明，TAK1沉默可减轻顺铂诱导的肾小管细胞损伤，且TAK1活性对CUR的保护作用至关重要。结论：CUR通过靶向TAK1并抑制MAPK和NF-kappaB通路，改善了顺铂触发的AKI。这些发现表明，CUR可能作为一种有前景的辅助药物，以克服顺铂的主要局限性。
